title: The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: A publicist can operate as institutional infrastructure by deciding what becomes legible, to whom, through which relationships and records—but narrative power must be governed through evidence, approvals, credit, access, correction, and ethical limits.
frames.alt: Title plate for The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · FRAME — What is the house asking the public to understand?. Write the evidenced proposition, intended audience, context, proof, exclusions, affected people, and correction condition. Separate a useful frame from a claim the available record cannot support.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what is the house asking the public to understand? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · RELATE — Which relationships carry the frame?. Map journalists, editors, critics, stylists, talent, institutions, buyers, creators, community authorities, platforms, and internal spokespeople. Record the purpose, relevant disclosure, access terms, embargo, conflicts, and who is excluded.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping which relationships carry the frame? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · GOVERN — Who may say, approve, reuse, and retain what?. Define scope of services, spokesperson authority, substantiation, review time, confidential information, identity and image permissions, media and territory, archive copies, post-term use, credit, correction, takedown, and termination from the actual agreement.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who may say, approve, reuse, and retain what? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · REMEMBER — What enters the institutional record?. Preserve final releases, pitches where appropriate, media lists under proper privacy controls, approvals, corrections, placements, refusals, captions, credits, rights evidence, and decision context. The archive should record how public meaning was made—not only the resulting coverage.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what enters the institutional record? within The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

frames.caption: Publicity can confer legitimacy while reproducing gatekeeping, extraction, favoritism, undisclosed influence, or historical erasure. More coverage is not automatically stronger institutional infrastructure. A responsible system must track who gains voice, who bears reputational risk, which claims are evidenced, and whether correction remains possible.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for The Publicist as Institutional Infrastructure.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery

frames.caption: Map every relationship carrying the story, including access, embargo, compensation or material connection, conflict, exclusion, and disclosure.
